title: Four ordinary purchases in an hour on the customer's trusted phone (velocity flag boundary)
narrative: An established customer pays $38.20 for groceries, their fourth purchase in the past hour, all at ordinary amounts, on their usual phone from their home IP in the billing country. Nothing else is unusual.
rationale: Several small purchases in an hour on a trusted device at home is ordinary shopping behaviour, not card testing: the amounts are normal and every identity and location signal is clean. Approval is the expected outcome; a light review is acceptable. Decline would be a false positive. Four purchases in an hour is exactly where the velocity tool's rapid-succession flag starts firing since the threshold changed from more than four to four or more, so this scenario puts that boundary under the evaluation.
